objective: Exploratory experiment: take the periodic planes PINWHEEL-ATLAS-20261107-001B tested and rejected uncut (rectangle grids and brick rows with diagonals of period up to 2 x 2, domino tilings of small tori with every diagonal choice, the six two-tile shapes tiled by half-turns), cut each one, two and three times, and test every tile's collar against the 108 complete pinwheel collars. Count which planes become collar-legal and after how many cuts.
status: Closed, supported (exploratory, COLLAR-PLANE-20261108-001C-E001): of PINWHEEL-ATLAS-20261107-001B's periodic planes, cut one to three times, only the rhombus lattice (in four presentations: checkerboard grids, the two isosceles shapes tiled by half-turns, eight domino tilings of the 2 x 4 and 4 x 2 tori) is collar-legal after one cut; six brick-row planes and 16 more domino tilings join after two cuts; every other plane fails (rectangle lattice, kite, parallelograms). The 2 x 6, 6 x 2 and 4 x 4 tori after one cut (95,232 planes) run in the background (collar-plane-c1, docs/LONG_RUNNING.md) and will be folded in.
title: Which tested periodic planes become pinwheel-legal after cutting
